chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: Drafted into the Army after an all-night Commodore session
summary: He cuts some of his best Commodore sides the night before reporting to Fort Dix in December 1943; Dunham promises him a job after the war.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: day or the night I was to go in the Army the following day and I went into Fort Dix and, uh, I had made some of the best sides that I have ever made for Commodore on that particular one. Of course, I came back from the Army and made some more Commodores - different times --
While you were still in the Army--
This was 1943 when you went in the Army---
---and you were 37 years old--- and so you got that---
---well, you went in in December - didn't you?
So, you went in -a matter of about two or three weeks before your 38th birthday---
And, of course you know - at that time in the war, they were letting a lot of guys out at 38---
I was just going to say - I think you would not have been drafted if it had been another three weeks gone by---
Yes but they found out I played the cornet - and I was in forever---
And, they decided they needed you --
No - Yeah - of course, I remember Katherine Dunham throwing her arms around me and saying - when you're out of all this - come back -- you'll have a job with me, but - of course, I never did that.
And, she had a couple of other shows during the time I was in the Army and then, of course, when I got back, she was doing something else--- so I never did that.
